title: Hypothesis-driven A/B framework and exposure scheduler for model versions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Engineering teams need a repeatable, low-friction way to run A/B experiments across model versions with deterministic exposure, guardrails for user safety, and automated rollback when quality regresses. Current canary tooling supports simple percentage ramps but lacks hypothesis definition, sample-size estimation, sequential statistical checks, and an exposure scheduler that respects business hours, cohorts, and tokens quotas.

Proposal: Deliver a Hypothesis-Driven A/B Framework and Exposure Scheduler as part of the Model Lifecycle Platform. Key capabilities: deterministic bucketing by user-id or request fingerprint; experiment API and Console UX to declare hypotheses (primary metric, direction, minimum detectable effect); built-in sample-size estimator; exposure scheduler for staged ramps, time-of-day constraints, cohort targeting, and shadow tap (mirror traffic to candidate variant without returning output); sequential statistical gatekeeper with configurable tests (e.g., Wald SPRT, sequential t-test), false-discovery control, and CI estimation; automatic action rules (promote, continue, pause, rollback) driven by configurable thresholds and cooldown windows; experiment artifacts stored as immutable records for auditing and compliance.

Integration points: uses rollout/traffic router for routing decisions, observability pipeline for metric ingestion, and the Console for experiment creation and reporting. Should emit audit logs for every exposure change and decision for Private deployments (KMS/HSM signing optional).

Why unique: We emphasize hypothesis-first experiments (not just traffic flips) and a scheduler that lets product teams align experiments with user activity and compliance windows. We also add a safety-first auto-rollback playbook that operates on multiple signals (quality regression, latency impact, cost delta).
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /experiments creates an experiment with name, hypothesis, primary metric, direction, effect_size, and exposure schedule
Console: UX flow to create staged exposure schedules (e.g., 0.5% -> 2% -> 10%) with time-of-day windows and cohort targeting
Deterministic bucketing: 99.99% stability across restarts using consistent hashing and seed storage
Statistical gatekeeper: sequential tests run on aggregated metrics and decide pass/fail according to configured thresholds within the expected sample window
Shadow tap: option to mirror 100% of production requests to candidate variant without influencing responses, with telemetry captured in the evaluation pipeline
Auto-rollback: rule engine triggers a rollback when primary metric delta <= -X% with p-value < configured_threshold and sustained for configured_cooldown
Observability: experiment dashboard displays cumulative delta, CI, sample size, and per-cohort slices; links to raw event streams and logs
Auditability: immutable experiment record and action logs available for export and review
E2E test: example experiment run in staging showing promotion from canary to full rollout and one intentional rollback scenario
notes: Design decision: default statistical method will be a sequential t-test with optional SPRT for low-latency experiments. We will expose method choice but provide conservative defaults.
Trade-off: strict statistical gating increases time to reach significance for small effect sizes; provide guidance and an estimator in the UI to set realistic effect_size and runtime expectations.
Performance: minimize per-request overhead by computing deterministic bucket in router and attaching experiment metadata to trace/span rather than synchronous calls to the experiment service.
Privacy: for Private deployments, allow bucketing by hashed customer_id stored only in HSM/KMS contexts if required by compliance.
Open question: how to combine multiple primary metrics (e.g., quality + latency + cost)? Proposed interim: composite score with configurable weights per experiment.

Rollout playbook: recommended defaults for rollback thresholds: quality delta <= -3% with p-value < 0.01 OR latency 95th percentile +20% sustained for 15 minutes. These are defaults only and configurable per experiment.
